title: cohort-steer: deterministic stitching and safe drift-correction for sampled canaries
author: Maya Gonzales
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently run sampled canaries and A/B experiments in parallel with shadow traffic for long-lived cohorts. Existing rollout controllers occasionally produce cohort jostle (users flip between lanes when sampling keys change) and silent drift where small model differences accumulate across sessions. This PR introduces 'cohort-steer', a deterministic stitching layer plus a lightweight drift-correction probe that: 1) deterministically maps identity keys to cohort lanes across sequential rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow) to avoid jostle, 2) tracks per-cohort micro-drift signals (response divergence + latency delta) and surfaces corrective actions to the rollout controller, and 3) integrates safety gates so rollback or traffic-hold triggers are automatic when drift exceeds configurable budgets.

What this changes (high level): - New Stitcher: a deterministic key hashing + affinity window that preserves cohort assignment across model swaps and sampling policy changes. - Drift probe: small in-band evaluation harness that computes session-consistent divergence metrics and emits signals to rollouts. - Controller integration: rollout controller consumes drift signals and supports timebox-based corrective staging (hold, revert, throttle). - Config surface: rollout policy gains two new knobs: "affinity_window" and "drift_budget" with sensible defaults. - Tests and e2e: unit tests for stitcher, integration tests with synthetic session replay to validate zero-jostle and rollback on drift.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1282) - [x] Unit tests for stitcher and probe - [x] Integration playback test against synthetic sessions - [x] Canary e2e scenario in perf-canary suite - [x] Docs update (console + API) - [x] Backward-compatible config defaults

Commits (summary): - 7b3c2d4: add deterministic cohort stitcher and affinity window implementation - 2a9b1f0: expose stitcher hooks to rollout controller and add config parsing - f1c8a7d: implement drift probe and metric emission (latency/divergence) - e5d4b62: safety gate wiring and automatic rollback path - a9f4b11: tests + integration playback fixtures - c3d2e90: docs and CLI examples

Changed files (high level): - rollout/controller/cohort_stitcher.py (+680 -12): deterministic mapping algorithm, affinity window logic, small inline docs - rollout/controller/rollout_controller.py (+210 -45): consumes drift signals, adds hold/revert APIs - rollout/config/policy_schema.yaml (+40 -0): new affinity_window/drift_budget fields and validation - runtime/telemetry/drift_probe.py (+320 -10): lightweight divergence probe, sampling hooks - tests/unit/test_cohort_stitcher.py (+120 -0) - tests/integration/test_drift_playback.py (+420 -10) - docs/rollouts/cohort-steer.md (+180 -2) - examples/rollout-samples/cohort-affinity.yaml (+24 -0)

Why this is safe: The stitcher is opt-in per-rollout (default affinity_window = 0 meaning no cross-rollout affinity), so existing behavior unchanged. Drift signals are advisory by default; automatic rollback requires an explicit drift_budget > 0 in the rollout spec. All new APIs are gated behind a feature flag rollout.experimental.cohortSteer (rolls out to canary controller first).

Rollout config example (short): rollout:
  name: search-canary
  strategy: canary
  cohortSteer:
    enabled: true
    affinity_window: 14d
    drift_budget:
      divergence_threshold: 0.03
      latency_p50_ms: 150

release_notes: Adds an opt-in cohort affinity feature that preserves user cohort assignments across sequential rollouts and introduces a drift-detection probe with automatic safety gates. Defaults are backward-compatible. See docs/rollouts/cohort-steer.md for configuration and operational guidance.
notes_for_backport: Non-breaking opt-in feature. Backport only if customers request affinity preservation on older release branches.
operational_impact: Feature gated; no automatic changes to existing rollouts. Adds new telemetry (rollout.cohort_drift_* metrics) and one small CPU microbenchmark for the stitcher. Recommended to enable in staging first.
